sections.en: 1 should it not be ποιηταί ('makers'), γῆς ... ἐπιτροπῆς τε καὶ ('of the earth ... and of the stewardship') ... namely σπορίμου ('of the sown'). 3 ὡς ἐπιπάντων γὰρ ('for as of all') M has. 5 concerning the tropical signs and the Midheaven and the Sun Firmicus has nothing, but nevertheless: munus praeclarae legationis inponunt, sed amittentes filios ... aut alienam sobolem nutrire coguntur aut... ('they impose the duty of a distinguished embassy, but losing their children ... they are compelled either to nourish another's offspring or...'). 8 τοῦ ('of the')] the dative is more frequent. 10 perhaps πρεσβευταὶ ὑπὲρ ('ambassadors on behalf of')? 15 τὲ ('and') as it seems has perished with the paper. 17 in stars seeing each other from a square (from a trine 174, 27) there is ἐπιδεκατεία καὶ καθυπερτέρησίς ('a tenth-part relation and overcoming'), ὅταν ἐν δεξιῷ τόπῳ ὑπάρχων τις τὸν ἐν τῷ ἀριστερῷ τριγώνῳ ἢ τετραγώνῳ ἢ ἑξαγώνῳ ἐπιθεωρῇ ('whenever one being in the right place observes the one in the left trine or square or hexagon') (Catal. cod. Flor., 157, 5). Cf. above at p. 162, 25, below 168, 8. ἐπικεῖθαι ('to lie upon') he says at 172, 29. 19 ἐγκοπτικός ('hindering') satisfies the sentence (actus impediunt ['they hinder actions'] Firmicus has, in whom all the same things are found). 23 perhaps δίδωσι ('gives')? 25-28 the same things Firmicus has, 72v a. 26 ἐπὶ ('upon')] perhaps περὶ ('concerning')? (ex casu filiorum acerba doloris tormenta ... indicit ['from the misfortune of children it indicates bitter torments of grief ...'], Firmicus has). 28 εὐτυχῆ ('fortunate')] δυστυχῆ ('unfortunate') M has.

summary.headline: Planetary Aspects and Life Fortune
summary.text: Astrological delineation of Hermes with Kronos and Zeus in trines, tropical signs, culmination, and aspects, including political offices, ambassadorship, guardianship, and inheritance. Squares and oppositions involving Ares, Kronos, and Zeus are interpreted for envy, losses, paternal harm, and changing fortunes across the stages of life.
